title: MSH — Message Header Segment
summary: The mandatory first segment of every HL7 v2 message — declares delimiters, message type, and control identifiers.

elements.name: Field Separator
elements.description: The character immediately following 'MSH' — defines the field separator for the entire message. Confirmed R (required) against the real HL7 Attribute Table.

elements.name: Encoding Characters
elements.description: Four characters in order: component, repetition, escape, subcomponent separators — conventionally ^~\&.

elements.name: Message Type
elements.description: Identifies the message type and trigger event, e.g. ADT^A01 — determines which segments follow.

elements.name: Message Control ID
elements.description: Unique identifier for this message instance, echoed back in MSA-2 of the acknowledgment.

elements.name: Processing ID
elements.description: Distinguishes production, training, and debugging traffic. Confirmed R (required) against the real HL7 Attribute Table.

elements.name: Version ID
elements.description: The HL7 version this message conforms to, e.g. 2.5.1. Corrected from an earlier 0..1 (optional) — the real HL7 Attribute Table confirms this is R (required), not optional.

content.fieldNotes: MSH-1 and MSH-2 are self-referential — MSH-1 is literally the character it defines, and MSH-2 is only readable once MSH-1 is known. Every downstream segment in the message depends on the delimiter set declared here, which is why MSH must always be first and why a malformed MSH breaks the entire message, not just one field. Full attribute table confirmed 2026-07-28 via DOM range extraction between heading anchors on the real v2.5.1 page (get_page_text truncates before reaching this table; direct DOM query does not).

title: MSA — Message Acknowledgment Segment
summary: Carries the outcome of a received message — the core of every ACK, referenced by every message type, not owned by any one of them.

elements.name: Acknowledgment Code
elements.description: AA/AE/AR for original-mode or application-level acks; CA/CE/CR for enhanced-mode accept acks.

elements.name: Message Control ID
elements.description: Echoes the original message's MSH-10 — this is what links an ACK back to the message it's acknowledging.

content.fieldNotes: An ACK message is intentionally minimal — MSH + MSA, optionally SFT and repeating ERR. It carries an outcome about another message, not new clinical or administrative data of its own. Full attribute table confirmed 2026-07-28: MSA-1 and MSA-2 both R (required), matching what was already recorded.

title: EVN — Event Type Segment
summary: Carries the triggering event's type and timing for ADT messages — always paired with MSH-9 for the same information in a different form.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 3 — Patient Administration

elements.name: Event Type Code
elements.description: Retained for backward compatibility — the trigger event is authoritatively carried in MSH-9, not here, in current implementations. Confirmed OPT=B (backward-compatibility designation specifically, not a general 'optional') against the real HL7 Attribute Table.

elements.name: Recorded Date/Time
elements.description: When the event was actually recorded in the sending system, which may differ from when it occurred. Corrected from an earlier 0..1 (optional) — the real HL7 Attribute Table confirms this is R (required).

content.fieldNotes: EVN-1 duplicating MSH-9's trigger event is a legacy artifact — don't build parsing logic that depends on EVN-1 being populated or matching MSH-9; treat MSH-9 as the source of truth for what kind of event this is. Cardinality for this segment's fields is standards-consistent inference, not confirmed against an explicit required/optional table cell — attempted 2026-07-27, source page truncated before reaching that column. Held at needs-review pending that specific check. Full attribute table confirmed 2026-07-28.

title: PID — Patient Identification Segment
summary: Carries patient demographic identity — the segment every ADT, Order, and Result message references back to.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 3 — Patient Administration

elements.name: Patient Identifier List
elements.description: One or more identifiers (e.g. MRN) for the patient — required, repeating.

elements.name: Patient Name
elements.description: Legal name and any aliases — required, repeating.

elements.name: Date/Time of Birth
elements.description: Optional, non-repeating. Corrected from an initial DTM claim — confirmed TS against the version-pinned v2.5.1 text; DTM was a harmonized-reference artifact.

elements.name: Administrative Sex
elements.description: Optional, non-repeating, coded per User-defined Table 0001. Corrected from an initial CWE claim — confirmed IS against the version-pinned v2.5.1 text.

content.fieldNotes: PID-3 and PID-5 are the two fields every downstream system actually depends on — everything else on this segment is context, not identity. Missing or malformed PID-3 is the single most common cause of a failed patient match downstream.

title: PV1 — Patient Visit Segment
summary: Carries visit-level data — where the patient is, who's treating them, what kind of encounter this is — distinct from PID's patient-identity data.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 3 — Patient Administration

elements.name: Patient Class
elements.description: I/O/E for inpatient/outpatient/emergency — coded per user-defined table 0004.

elements.name: Assigned Patient Location
elements.description: Point-of-care/room/bed — where the patient currently is, not where they were admitted.

elements.name: Attending Doctor
elements.description: The physician(s) of record for this visit. Corrected from an earlier 0..1 (single) — the real HL7 Attribute Table confirms RP/#=Y (repeating), consistent with a visit having more than one attending physician of record.

elements.name: Visit Number
elements.description: The identifier for this specific visit/encounter, distinct from PID-3's patient-level identifiers.

content.fieldNotes: PV1-19 is the visit-level identifier — this is the field that maps most directly to FHIR's Encounter.id/identifier, while PID-3 maps to Patient's identity. Conflating the two is a common source of matching errors when two systems disagree about which ID scopes a record. Cardinality for this segment's fields is standards-consistent inference, not confirmed against an explicit required/optional table cell — attempted 2026-07-27, source page truncated before reaching that column. Held at needs-review pending that specific check. Full attribute table confirmed 2026-07-28.

title: NK1 — Next of Kin / Associated Parties Segment
summary: Carries next-of-kin or other associated-party information — optional and repeating, attached to a patient but not required for a valid ADT message.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 3 — Patient Administration

elements.name: Set ID - NK1
elements.description: Sequence number distinguishing repeated NK1 occurrences within one message.

elements.name: Name
elements.description: The associated party's name. Corrected from an earlier 0..1 (single) — the real HL7 Attribute Table confirms RP/#=Y (repeating).

elements.name: Relationship
elements.description: Coded relationship to the patient (spouse, parent, guardian, etc.) — confirmed CE, not the newer CWE, at v2.5.1.

content.fieldNotes: Zero, one, or many NK1 segments can appear per message — never assume exactly one is present, and never treat an absent NK1 as an error. NK1-3's data type is a documented trip-wire: a harmonized-reference search will report CWE; the actual v2.5.1 text says CE. Cardinality for this segment's fields is standards-consistent inference, not confirmed against an explicit required/optional table cell — attempted 2026-07-27, source page truncated before reaching that column. Held at needs-review pending that specific check. Full attribute table confirmed 2026-07-28.

title: ORC — Common Order Segment
summary: Carries order-control status and identity shared across all order types — paired with a type-specific detail segment like OBR.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 4 — Order Entry

elements.name: Order Control
elements.description: What's happening to this order — NW (new), CA (cancel), OK (accepted), etc. This is what actually drives order-workflow logic, not the message type alone.

elements.name: Placer Order Number
elements.description: Assigned by the ordering system. Either this or OBR-2 must be present; when both are present they should match.

elements.name: Filler Order Number
elements.description: Assigned by the fulfilling system. Either this or OBR-3 must be present.

elements.name: Date/Time of Transaction
elements.description: When this specific order-control event occurred.

content.fieldNotes: ORC-1 is the field that actually tells you what kind of order event this is — don't infer order state from the message type (ORM/OMG) alone, since one message can carry multiple order-control actions across repeating ORC groups.

title: OBR — Observation Request Segment
summary: Report-header segment shared by order messages and ORU results — restates order identity and the service being requested or reported on.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 7 — Observation Reporting

elements.name: Placer Order Number
elements.description: Conditional — required if ORC-2 isn't present in the same order group.

elements.name: Filler Order Number
elements.description: Conditional — required if ORC-3 isn't present; ORC itself is optional in ORU, so this is often the only place the filler number appears.

elements.name: Universal Service Identifier
elements.description: The test or procedure being ordered/reported — confirmed CE, not CWE, at v2.5.1.

elements.name: Observation Date/Time
elements.description: Conditional — when the observation was actually made, distinct from when it was ordered.

elements.name: Ordering Provider
elements.description: Who ordered this — often restated here even though it's implied by the originating order.

content.fieldNotes: OBR is the segment most worth remembering as reused, not duplicated — the same segment definition appears inside an order message and as ORU's report header. OBR-4's data type is another CE/CWE trip-wire instance, same pattern as PID-8 and NK1-3.

title: OBX — Observation/Result Segment
summary: Carries a single discrete measurement or finding — an OBR report header is followed by one OBX per observation.

sourceOfTruth.title: HL7 Version 2.5.1 Standard, Chapter 7 — Observation Reporting

elements.name: Value Type
elements.description: Declares which HL7 data type OBX-5 is encoded as (NM, ST, CE, etc.) — required to correctly parse OBX-5 at all.

elements.name: Observation Identifier
elements.description: What was measured, typically coded against LOINC. Confirmed CE, not CWE, at v2.5.1 — this field was left flagged as contradictory in an earlier review pass and is now resolved against the version-pinned table.

elements.name: Observation Value
elements.description: The actual result — its data type is whatever OBX-2 declared, not fixed.

elements.name: Observation Result Status
elements.description: P/F/C/etc. — preliminary, final, corrected. Downstream systems should treat a corrected result as superseding a prior final one with the same OBX-3, not as a new, unrelated finding.

content.fieldNotes: OBX-2 has to be read before OBX-5 can be parsed correctly — this is the field-level version of the same self-referential pattern MSH-1/MSH-2 have at the message level. A single OBR can be followed by many OBX segments, one per discrete measurement.

title: GET [base]/metadata
summary: Retrieves a server's CapabilityStatement — what resources and interactions it actually supports, discovered at runtime rather than assumed from documentation.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Optional. full (default) | normative | terminology — controls how much of the CapabilityStatement is returned.

content.fieldNotes: This is the block that resolves capability 7's discovery mechanism — before assuming a server supports a given resource or interaction, check its CapabilityStatement rather than the spec alone, since spec compliance and server implementation are two different things. Returns 404 if the endpoint doesn't speak FHIR at all, which is itself useful information.

title: Patient
summary: The person receiving care — a standalone, referenceable resource, not a segment embedded in a message.

elements.name: identifier
elements.description: Business identifiers (MRN, SSN, etc.) — the FHIR analogue of PID-3, generalized to any identifier scheme.

elements.name: name
elements.description: Repeating — supports multiple names/aliases.

elements.name: gender
elements.description: Bound to a required-strength ValueSet — administrative gender, not clinical sex.

content.fieldNotes: Same identity function as v2's PID, but as its own addressable resource other resources reference by URL rather than a segment that only exists inside one message. gender here is administrative, not a clinical/biological claim — a common point of confusion worth calling out explicitly.

title: GET [base]/Patient/{id}
summary: Retrieves a single Patient resource instance by its logical id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's logical id, assigned by the server on create

content.fieldNotes: This is the same shape as a Cisco show command — a request and a real response — which is why this specific corner of FHIR stayed InvokableContent instead of needing the Structural shape the resources themselves required.

title: Encounter
summary: Represents when and where care happened — the standalone, referenceable analogue of v2's PV1.

elements.name: status
elements.description: planned | arrived | triaged | in-progress | onleave | finished | cancelled + — required.

elements.name: class
elements.description: Classification of the encounter (inpatient/outpatient/emergency/etc.) — the closest analogue to v2's PV1-2 Patient Class, though not bound to the same table.

elements.name: subject
elements.description: Who this encounter is for.

elements.name: participant
elements.description: People involved in the encounter (attending, consulting, etc.) — generalizes PV1-7's single Attending Doctor field into a repeating, typed list.

elements.name: period
elements.description: Start and end time of the encounter.

elements.name: reasonCode
elements.description: Coded reason the encounter happened.

elements.name: serviceProvider
elements.description: The organization responsible for this encounter.

content.fieldNotes: class is a single Coding, not a CodeableConcept — it's meant to carry one system-defined classification, not a list of candidate codes. participant generalizing PV1-7 into a repeating, role-typed structure is the concrete example of the paradigm shift capability 7 describes: v2 gives you one named field per role it anticipated, FHIR gives you a repeating structure that doesn't need a new field for a new role.

title: Observation
summary: A measurement or point-in-time assessment — the structural analogue of v2's OBX, generalized well beyond lab results.

elements.name: status
elements.description: registered | preliminary | final | amended + — the FHIR analogue of OBX-11's result status.

elements.name: code
elements.description: What was observed — the analogue of OBX-3, typically bound to LOINC.

elements.name: subject
elements.description: Who or what the observation is about.

elements.name: encounter
elements.description: The encounter this observation was made during.

elements.name: effective[x]
elements.description: When the observed value is asserted true — the analogue of OBR-7/OBX-14.

elements.name: value[x]
elements.dataType: Quantity | CodeableConcept | string | boolean | integer | Range | Ratio | SampledData | time | dateTime | Period
elements.description: The result itself — its type varies by choice-of-type suffix, the direct analogue of OBX-2 declaring OBX-5's type.

elements.name: interpretation
elements.description: High/low/normal flag — roughly analogous to OBX-8 (Abnormal Flags).

content.fieldNotes: value[x] and effective[x] are FHIR's 'choice of type' pattern — the actual field name in an instance is valueQuantity, valueString, etc., never literally 'value[x]'. This is the same self-referential-typing idea as OBX-2/OBX-5, just expressed as a naming convention instead of a separate declaring field.

title: ServiceRequest
summary: A request for a service to be performed — the analogue of v2's order (ORC/OBR territory).

elements.name: status
elements.description: draft | active | on-hold | revoked | completed | entered-in-error | unknown — the analogue of ORC-1's order-control state, though not a 1:1 value mapping.

elements.name: intent
elements.description: proposal | plan | order | original-order | reflex-order | etc. — distinguishes an actual order from a plan or proposal, a distinction v2's ORC-1 doesn't separate out as its own field.

elements.name: code
elements.description: The service being requested — the analogue of OBR-4's Universal Service Identifier.

elements.name: subject
elements.description: Who or what the service is for — required, unlike Observation.subject.

elements.name: encounter
elements.description: The encounter this request was made during.

elements.name: requester
elements.dataType: Reference(Practitioner | PractitionerRole | Organization | Patient | RelatedPerson | Device)
elements.description: Who initiated the request — the analogue of OBR-16's Ordering Provider, but typed to allow non-practitioner requesters too.

elements.name: occurrence[x]
elements.description: When the requested service should happen.

content.fieldNotes: ServiceRequest.subject is required (1..1) where Observation.subject and Encounter.subject are both optional (0..1) — a service request without a subject genuinely doesn't make sense the way an Observation about aggregate/population data sometimes can. Worth knowing as the one cardinality difference across these three resources that isn't just modeling convenience.
